name: presentation
title: Presentation
description: A .pptx viewer: a numbered thumbnail rail down the left, a large auto-fitted slide on the right, and in-slide selection with resize and rotate handles. Clicking a thumbnail flips the deck.
use: Users need to open and page through a real .pptx deck inside the app, optionally editing slide objects.
avoid: It leans on a separate .pptx parser, needs a container with real height, and shows nothing until a deck loads.
a11y: Thumbnails take focus and the mobile rail has labels, but slide object keyboard support comes from the underlying package and nothing checks reduced motion. (keyboard: partial, labels: partial, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A bordered app panel with a thin toolbar and a file picker. Down the left runs a column of small numbered slide previews; the rest is a large framed slide canvas showing cream pages with serif headlines and thin rules, or dark green cover slides.
behaves: Clicking a thumbnail swaps the big slide and the viewport refits it to the space. Inside a slide, objects can be marquee-selected, dragged, resized and rotated with handles; on narrow screens the rail slides out from behind a toggle button.
customise: Give the provider a store loaded from a .pptx buffer, then compose the thumbnail list, content, viewport and slide. Every part takes a className and replacement children.
weight: heavy: Parses a .pptx file and renders every slide plus a thumbnail for each, so cost grows with deck size.
